2022|access-date=24 May 2022}} It advocates for lower taxation, [[Anti-abortion movement|anti-abortion]] measures and [[Austerity|austerity cuts]]. It was founded as the '''Conservative Party''' in August 2011 by businessman and political activist [[Colin Craig]], who led the party from its foundation until his resignation in June 2015.{{cite news|title=Conservative Party's Colin Craig stands down|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/276656/conservative-party%27s-colin-craig-stands-down|access-date=4 July 2017|work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=19 June 2015|language=en-nz}} The party had two members on the [[Upper Harbour Local Board]] in [[Auckland]] from 2013 to 2016. The party has contested the four [[Elections in New Zealand|general elections]] from [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011]] through [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020]] without winning any seats. At the 2014 election it received 3.97% of the vote. At the 2020 general election, they gained 1.5% of the vote. The party changed its name to '''New Conservative''' in November 2017,{{cite web|date=12 December 2017|title=Conservative Party to Get New Name|url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1712/S00112/conservative-party-to-get-new-name.htm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904040224/http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1712/S00112/conservative-party-to-get-new-name.htm|archive-date=4 September 2019|access-date=6 August 2018|publisher=Scoop.co.nz}} and then to New Conservatives in 2023. ===Colin Craig era, 2011–2016=== ====Formation==== The Conservative Party was founded by Colin Craig, a businessman who had organised a protest march in 2009{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10741939|title=Dreams of Act's demise|last=Fisher|first=David|date=31 July 2011|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] }}{{cite Herald]] |access-date=29 September 2011}} and who had stood in the [[2010 Auckland mayoral election]], polling third with 8.7% of the vote.Craig received 42,598 votes behind Len Brown (237,487 votes) and John Banks (171,542 votes): {{cite web |url = http://www.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz/EN/AboutCouncil/HowCouncilWorks/Elections/Pages/Finalresults-Mayor.aspx |title = Mayor (1) final results |work = Conservative Party |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=3 August 2011 |access-date=3 August 2011}} at a media event in Newmarket, Auckland.{{cite news| url= joined it, indicated by the change in colour here.]] ====2011 election==== The Conservatives contested the [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011 general election]]. In October 2011 they announced electoral alliances with [[The Kiwi Party]] and [[New Citizen Party]], in which their candidates stood instead as Conservatives.{{cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=10759055 |title=No Kiwi Party candidates in this year's election |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=14 October 2011 |access-date=16 October 2011}}{{cite web |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/5807380/New-Citizens-Party-joins-with-Conservatives |title=New Citizens Party joins with Conservatives |author=Danya Levy |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=18 October 2011 |access-date=18 October 2011}} The party ran a list of 52 candidates, including Kiwi Party leader [[Larry Baldock]] and former New Citizen [[Botany (New Zealand electorate)|Botany]] candidate Paul Young.{{cite web |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1111/S00014/conservative-list-released.htm |title=Conservative list released |publisher=Press Release: Conservative Party (via Scoop.co.nz) |date=1 November 2011 |access-date=1 November 2011}} Craig stood in the [[Rodney (New Zealand electorate)|Rodney]] electorate.{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10752761|title=Colin Craig won't go up against John Banks|date=19 September 2011|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=19 September 2011}} The party spent NZ$1.88 million on its campaign, the second-highest of any party,{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10794298|title=Conservatives got least bang for buck|last=Young|first=Audrey|date=24 March 2012|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=24 March 2012}} with most of the money coming from Craig himself.{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=10767788|title=Election 2011: Craig spends $1 million to push his new party's plans|date=22 November 2011|work=[[New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=27 November 2011}} During the campaign the party portrayed itself as able to work with either of the two main parties, [[New Zealand National Party|National]] and [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour]].{{cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=10765411 |title=Conservative Party still working on major policies |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=11 November 2011 |access-date=27 November 2011}} It highlighted its socially conservative policies of raising the [[drinking age]] to 21, parental notification for abortions, and repeal of the [[Crimes (Substituted Section 59) Amendment Act 2007|"anti-smacking" law]]. It announced its opposition to National's policy of selling state assets. The party gained 2.65% of the [[party vote]] (59,237 votes), but failed to win any seats in Parliament.{{cite web |url=http://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2011/partystatus.html |title=Official count results – overall status |publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission |date=17 December 2011 |access-date=24 March 2012}} Craig came second in Rodney, gaining 8,031 votes – 12,222 votes behind first-time National Party candidate [[Mark Mitchell (New Zealand politician)|Mark Mitchell]].{{cite web|url=http://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2011/electorate-44.html |title=Official count results – Rodney |publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission |date=10 December 2011 |access-date=24 March 2012}} Following the election, Conservative candidates Larry Baldock and Peter Redman were referred to police for filing false expenses returns and for exceeding the $25,000 cap on election expenses.{{cite web |url=http://www.elections.org.nz/news-media/referral-police-16-april-2013 |title=Referral to the Police 16 April 2013 |publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission |date=16 April 2013 |access-date=16 April 2013}} Colin Craig stated that if the police found any impropriety neither Larry Baldock nor Peter Redman would be allowed to stand as Conservative candidates. The police subsequently declined to lay charges in the matter.{{citation needed|date=August 2014}} ====2011 to 2014==== [[File:Colin Craig.JPG|thumb|right|Colin Craig, founder and first leader of the Conservative Party, 2011–2016]] In May 2013, the party appointed [[Christine Rankin]], a high-profile former [[Ministry of Social Development (New Zealand)|Work and Income New Zealand]] chief executive, as its own chief executive.{{cite web |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1305/S00131/conservative-partys-new-ceo-christine-rankin.htm |title=Conservative Party's new CEO Christine Rankin |publisher=Conservative Party |date=10 May 2013 |access-date=28 August 2014}} The party contested the [[2013 Christchurch East by-election]]; candidate Leighton Baker polled 494 votes (or 3.6%).{{Cite web|title=Official Count Results – Christchurch East|url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2013_christchurch_east_byelection/|website=electionresults.govt.nz}} The party also contested the [[2013 New Zealand local elections|2013 local elections]], fielding 27 candidates in [[Auckland]].{{cite web |url=http://www.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz/EN/AboutCouncil/HowCouncilWorks/Elections/Documents/lbfinalresults2013.pdf |title=Local boards final results |publisher=Auckland Council |date=17 October 2013}}{{cite web |url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/regional/216328/conservative-party-to-contest-auckland-elections |title=Conservative Party to contest Auckland elections|date=7 August 2013 |publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]}} The party gained 50,218 votes overall, and two candidates (Christine Rankin and Callum Blair) were elected to the [[Upper Harbour Local Board]].{{cite web |url=http://www.vote.co.nz/2013/elections/auckland-council-upper-harbour-local-board |title=Auckland Council – Upper Harbour Local Board |publisher=Local Government Online |access-date=28 August 2014}} In February 2014, the then-[[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green Party]] co-leader [[Russel Norman]] spoke at the [[Big Gay Out]] event in Auckland and alleged that Colin Craig held misogynistic and homophobic attitudes. In response, Craig filed a defamation suit and demanded that Norman issue an apology. Norman and the Green Party announced that they would contest the lawsuit.{{cite news|last1=Davison|first1=Isaac|title=Colin Craig to limit his defamation claim|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11213649|access-date=11 August 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=4 March 2015}} On 10 October 2014, the parties settled the lawsuit out of court and agreed to bear their own legal expenses.{{cite news|last1=Wong|first1=Simon|title=Colin Craig drops defamation case against Russel Norman|url=http://www.3news.co.nz/nznews/colin-craig-drops-defamation-case-against-russel-norman-2014101015#axzz3iY3Nkw7R|access-date=11 August 2015|publisher=3 News|date=10 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205225911/http://www.3news.co.nz/nznews/colin-craig-drops-defamation-case-against-russel-norman-2014101015#axzz3iY3Nkw7R|archive-date=5 December 2014|url-status=dead}} ====2014 election==== In November 2013, speculation arose in New Zealand news media{{cite news | last = Edwards |first = Bryce | title = Bryce Edwards: Political roundup: Winning at the 2014 general election |url = http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11163647 | work =[[New Zealand Herald]] | date = 27 November 2013 | access-date = 21 September 2014}} about a possible accommodation between the Conservatives and the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]] for the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]]. Comments by Prime Minister and National Party leader [[John Key]] led to speculation of a coalition in which the National Party would not run a candidate in an electorate on Auckland's [[North Shore City|North Shore]], such as [[Rodney (New Zealand electorate)|Rodney]], [[East Coast Bays (New Zealand electorate)|East Coast Bays]],{{cite web|last=Hooton|first=Matthew|title=National Must Gift East Coast Bays to Colin Craig|url=http://www.nbr.co.nz/article/hooton-on-colin-craig|access-date=4 December 2013|date=22 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140103025538/http://www.nbr.co.nz/article/hooton-on-colin-craig|archive-date=3 January 2014|url-status=dead}} or the newly formed {{NZ electorate link|Upper Harbour}}.{{cite web|title = Changes Proposed to Electorate Boundaries |url= http://www.elections.org.nz/news-media/changes-proposed-electorate-boundaries-0 |publisher=Electoral Commission|access-date=21 November 2013}} This would have assisted the Conservative Party in meeting the [[MMP in New Zealand|threshold]] for entering parliament. Ultimately, National ran candidates in all these electorates. http://www.3news.co.nz/Colin-Craig-undecided-on-electorate/tabid/1607/articleID/335060/Default.aspx}} Craig elected to stand in the East Coast Bays electorate.{{cite news|last1 = Bennett| first1 = Adam| date = 22 June 2014| title = Colin Craig to contest McCully for East Coast Bays seat| url = http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11279380| newspaper =[[The New Zealand Herald]] | location = Auckland| publisher = APN New Zealand Limited| issn = 1170-0777| access-date = 18 July 2014| quote = Conservative Party leader Colin Craig has confirmed he will contest Murray McCully's East Coast Bays seat in the September election.}} John Key announced on 28 July 2014 that the National party candidate for East Coast Bays, [[Murray McCully]], would not step aside to assist the Conservatives into parliament, nor would National urge its members to vote for Craig.{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11300193 |title=PM: No clear run for Conservatives |author=Derek Cheng, Claire Trevett |work=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=28 July 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}} Among its candidates, the Conservative Party selected its chief executive [[Christine Rankin]] to stand in the [[Epsom (New Zealand electorate)|Epsom electorate]]{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11303390 |title=Christine Rankin to stand for Conservatives in Epsom |author=Derek Cheng |work=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=3 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}} and [[Sensible Sentencing Trust]] founder [[Garth McVicar]]{{cite web|author=Isaac Davison|date=7 August 2014|title=Garth McVicar to stand for Conservative Party|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11305416|access-date=10 August 2014|work=[[New Zealand Herald]] }} for the [[Napier (New Zealand electorate)|Napier electorate]]. The Electoral Commission awarded the Conservatives $60,000 in advertising funding for the 2014 general election, three times the $20,800 allocation it made to the Conservatives in 2011.{{cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11269245|title=Advertising funding down for Nats, Labour; up for Greens, NZ First|date=7 June 2014|publisher=[[New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=10 August 2014}} On 1 August 2014, Colin Craig revealed that China-based firm Shanghai Pengxin was purchasing Lochinver Station, a large dairy farm, and said that the Conservatives were opposed to the deal.{{cite web|author=Isaac Davison|date=1 August 2014|title=Crafar farms buyers in new $70 million land deal|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/news/article.cfm?c_id=3&objectid=11302623|access-date=10 August 2014|work=[[New Zealand Herald]] }} The party reached 4.6% in a 3 News Reid Research poll released in late August 2014, suggesting that it might break the 5% threshold.{{cite web |url=http://www.3news.co.nz/politics/conservatives-close-to-parliament-in-new-poll-2014082714 |title=Conservatives close to Parliament in new poll |publisher=3 News |date=27 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}}{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11315119 |title=National, Labour fall, minor parties rise in poll |author=Derek Cheng |publisher=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=27 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}} On 13 September, a TVNZ [[Colmar Brunton]] Poll showed McVicar polling 22% in the Napier electorate, behind both the Labour and National candidates.{{cite news|date=15 September 2014|title=Labour's Nash in the lead: poll|work=[[Hawke's Bay Today]] |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/hawkes-bay-today/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503462&objectid=11324800|access-date=21 September 2014}} The party was to be excluded from a televised debate of minor party leaders, while lower-polling parties such as [[ACT New Zealand]] and [[United Future]] would have been included. Craig won a High Court injunction on 8 August 2014 to prevent this exclusion, and ultimately appeared in the debate.{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11305906 |title=Colin Craig wins court scrap over TV3 debate |author=Rob Kidd |publisher=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=8 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}} Shortly before the general election, the party's press secretary Rachel MacGregor resigned, citing Colin Craig's alleged manipulative behaviour.{{cite news|last1=Dougan|first1=Patrick|title=Colin Craig's press secretary quits, reportedly calls him a 'manipulative man'|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11326951|access-date=21 June 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=18 September 2014}} The Conservative Party received 3.97% of the party vote and won no electorate seats, meaning that it did not meet the threshold to enter Parliament.{{cite news|last1=Sincock|first1=Taylor|title=Craig: Next election will be the one|url=http://www.3news.co.nz/politics/craig-next-election-will-be-the-one-2014092023#axzz3dfMEfax4|access-date=21 June 2015|agency=[[3 News]]|date=20 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150621081218/http://www.3news.co.nz/politics/craig-next-election-will-be-the-one-2014092023#axzz3dfMEfax4|archive-date=21 June 2015|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/partystatus.html|title=Election Results 2014|publisher=Electoral Commission|access-date=27 November 2014}} ====2015 resignations of leader and board members==== On 19 June 2015, Colin Craig resigned as leader of the Conservative Party's leader. Board members had scheduled a meeting for that day to discuss the leadership as it was felt that Craig's recent participation in a television interview (with [[David Farrier]] on the debut episode of ''[[Newsworthy (TV programme)|Newsworthy]]''), conducted in a sauna, had reflected badly on the party. Dissatisfaction had also been expressed over Craig's demeanour toward the party's former press secretary Rachel MacGregor, who had resigned just before the 2014 general election. Dissatisfaction increased when Craig pre-emptively and perhaps unconstitutionally postponed the meeting for a week in order to announce his resignation.{{cite news|last1=Farrier|first1=David|title=The Sauna Session That May Bring Down Colin Craig|url=http://www.3news.co.nz/tvshows/newsworthy/sauna-session-with-colin-craig-2015060823#axzz3dYJsninl|access-date=19 June 2015|agency=[[3 News]]|date=9 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620024928/http://www.3news.co.nz/tvshows/newsworthy/sauna-session-with-colin-craig-2015060823#axzz3dYJsninl|archive-date=20 June 2015|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|last1=Young|first1=Audrey|title=Colin Craig could face the chop after TV antics|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11467479|access-date=19 June 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=19 June 2015}}{{cite news|last1=Kirk|first1=Stacey|title=Conservative faction to block Colin Craig's return as leader|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/69559312/conservative-faction-to-block-colin-craigs-return-as-leader|access-date=19 June 2015|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=19 June 2015}} On 21 June, ''[[The New Zealand Herald]]'' reported that Craig had settled the dispute with MacGregor for around NZ$16,000 to NZ$17,000 eight weeks earlier.{{cite news|last1=Bilbey|first1=Lynley|title=Colin Craig entangled in money dispute|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11468628|access-date=21 June 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=21 July 2015}} [[One News (New Zealand)|One News]] also reported that there was a disagreement between Craig and several of the party's board members. One member, John Stringer, accused Craig of not following the party's constitution. Craig denied the allegation and threatened to take action against Stringer. The chairman of the Board stated that Stringer's views did not reflect the view of the Conservative Party and that his comments were only his opinion.{{cite web|date=21 June 2015|title=Colin Craig claims evidence of allegations withheld by Conservative Party|url=http://tvnz.co.nz/national-news/colin-craig-claims-evidence-allegations-withheld-conservative-party-6342837|access-date=21 June 2015|agency=[[One News (New Zealand)|One News]]}} That same day, Craig said that he would consider contesting the party's leadership if he had enough support.{{cite news|last1=Watkins|first1=Tracey|date=21 June 2015|title=Colin Craig off to lawyers, would consider a Conservative Party comeback|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/69567213/colin-craig-off-to-lawyers-would-consider-a-conservative-party-comeback|access-date=21 June 2015}} In a media conference on 22 June 2015, Craig admitted that he had "acted inappropriately" toward his press secretary Rachel MacGregor but denied any charge of sexual harassment. In response, MacGregor said that by making the admission, Craig had breached a confidentiality agreement the pair had reached under Human Rights Commission mediation and she disputed his account of the events. Craig's wife Helen Craig said that she was standing by her husband and characterized the charges against him as "false allegations."{{cite news|title=Colin Craig admits 'inappropriate' conduct|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/69601091/colin-craig-admits-inappropriate-conduct|access-date=22 June 2015|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=22 June 2015}}{{cite news|title='Factual inaccuracies' – former press secretary speaks out after Colin Craig denies allegations|url=http://tvnz.co.nz/national-news/factual-inaccuracies-former-press-secretary-speaks-after-colin-craig-denies-allegations-6343893|access-date=22 June 2015|agency=[[One News (New Zealand)|One News]]|date=22 June 2015}} According to the ''Herald'', several board members of the party including Stringer, [[Christine Rankin]], and Laurence Day indicated support for a change of leadership. A board meeting was scheduled for 27 June 2015 and Day called for Craig to be expelled from the party. Rankin, Garth McVicar, and [[Bob McCoskrie]] all ruled out contesting the leadership.{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11469194|title=Calls for Colin Craig's party membership to be cancelled|date=22 June 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|last1=Davison|first1=Isaac|access-date=22 June 2015}} In the week after Craig's resignation, all remaining members of the board apart from Stringer resigned. On 27 June 2015, at the scheduled board meeting, Stringer appointed a new board consisting of himself as chairman and four new members. This board voted to suspend Craig's membership in the party. Stringer said that a final decision about Craig's membership and the appointment of a new leader would be made at a later date.{{cite news|title=Colin Craig's membership suspended|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11472161}} According to One News, Craig later challenged the legality of Stringer's and the board's actions, claiming that Stringer had been suspended from the party. He did not rule out contesting the leadership. Craig's remarks were dismissed by Stringer, who became the party's interim leader.{{cite news|title=Colin Craig has Conservative Party membership suspended |url=http://tvnz.co.nz/national-news/colin-craig-has-conservative-party-membership-suspended-6347983 |access-date=27 June 2015 |publisher=[[One News (New Zealand)|One News]]|date=27 June 2015}} On 5 July 2015, Stringer resigned as chairman and as a board member, following statements that he had been suspended from the party and was therefore not entitled to hold them. According to the ''New Zealand Herald'', a statement had been made by former chairman Brian Dobbs that Stringer had been suspended, and this meant that the decision by the interim board to suspend Craig's membership was invalid.{{cite web | url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11476110 | access-date=6 July 2015 | title=Conservative Party battle draws to a close | date=5 July 2015 | publisher=[[The New Zealand Herald]] }} On 7 July, Craig sent a personal letter to Conservative Party members to apologise for his behaviour and to gauge whether he had sufficient support to return to the party's leadership.{{cite news|title=Colin Craig asks for forgiveness|url=http://www.odt.co.nz/news/politics/348330/colin-craig-asks-forgiveness|access-date=10 July 2015|publisher=[[Otago Daily Times]]|date=7 July 2015}}{{cite news|last1=Kirk|first1=Stacey|title=Colin Craig asks forgiveness and puts his political future to a ballot|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/70035019/colin-craig-asks-forgiveness-and-puts-his-political-future-to-a-ballot|access-date=10 July 2015|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=7 July 1025}} On 26 July 2015, a [[3News]]-Reid Research poll reported that support for the party was 0.7 per cent, the lowest it had polled since just before the 2011 general election.{{cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11486938 | access-date=26 July 2015 | title=Conservative Party support plunges to all-time low | date=26 July 2015 | publisher=[[The New Zealand Herald]] }} On 29 July 2015, Craig started a lawsuit against several opponents including the [[New Zealand Taxpayers' Union]]'s executive director [[Jordan Williams (New Zealand lawyer)|Jordan Williams]], fellow party member John Stringer, and the right wing blogger [[Cameron Slater]] for alleged defamation. Craig also circulated a booklet, titled ''Dirty Politics and Hidden Agendas'', in which he outlined a "campaign of defamatory lies" against him.{{cite news|last1=Miller|first1=Corazon|last2=Davison|first2=Isaac|title=Colin Craig sues 'dirty politics brigade'|url=http://m.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11488774|access-date=11 August 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=29 July 2015}}{{cite press release |last=Craig |first=Colin |date=2015 |title=Dirty Politics and Hidden Agendas |url=http://votecolincraig.co.nz/documents/Dirty%20Politics.pdf |location=Auckland |publisher=Colin and Helen Craig |access-date=11 August 2015 |url-status=dead Craig documents given to police|url=http://www.3news.co.nz/nznews/colin-craig-documents-given-to-police-2015081115#axzz3iY3Nkw7R|access-date=11 August 2015|agency=3 News|date=11 August On 14 August 2015, Jordan Williams launched a counter-suit against Craig and several Conservative Party officials in response to Craig's statements at the July press conference and in the circular ''Dirty Politics and Hidden Agendas''.{{cite news|last1=Jones|first1=Nicholas|title=Legal action taken against Colin Craig|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11497297|access-date=16 August 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=14 August 2015}} On 11 September 2015, Craig filed a retaliatory defamation suit against the party's former chairman, John Stringer. Stringer indicated that he would contest the charges in court.{{cite news|title=Colin Craig files defamation suit|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/283990/colin-craig-files-defamation-suit|access-date=11 October 2015|publisher=Radio New Zealand News|date=11 September 2015}} On 16 November 2015, Craig announced that he would not be contesting the Conservative Party leadership in light of a police investigation against him over his party's spending during the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]]. Craig also cited the ongoing lawsuits involving him, Cameron Slater, and Stringer as other reasons for his decision not to contest the party leadership.{{cite news|last1=Davidson|first1=Isaac|title=Colin Craig won't seek re-election|url=http://m.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11546300|access-date=17 November 2015|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=16 November 2015}} In addition, the newly elected Conservative Party board chair Leighton Baker indicated that the party was "in no hurry" to appoint a new leadership until it had rebuilt its membership base.{{cite news|last1=Kirk|first1=Stacey|title=Colin Craig not seeking re-election as Conservative Party leader|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/74089024/colin-craig-not-seeking-reelection-as-conservative-party-leader|access-date=17 November 2015|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=16 November 2015}} Ultimately, the police investigation cleared Craig of any wrongdoing.{{Citation needed|date=January 2022}} ====Legal strife and Colin Craig's resignation, 2016==== On 19 January 2016, Colin Craig donated NZ$36,000 to the Conservative Party. Despite his lack of involvement with the leadership, he stated that he and his wife still wanted to support the party financially.{{cite news|last1=Sachdeva|first1=Sam|title=Colin Craig donates $36,000 to Conservative Party after resigning as leader|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/76001561/colin-craig-donates-36000-to-conservative-party-after-resigning-as-leader|access-date=3 February 2016|publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=19 February 2016}} On 2 February 2016, the party's board validated the decision of the previous board to suspend John Stringer's membership. The suspension was part of an ongoing internal conflict within the party between Stringer and former party leader Craig.{{cite news|last1=Marwick|first1=Felix|title=Stringer's Conservative Party suspension confirmed|url=http://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/politics/stringers-conservative-party-suspension-confirmed/|access-date=3 February 2016|agency=[[Newstalk ZB]] |date=2 February 2016}} On 1 March 2016, it was reported that Stringer had dropped his defamation suit against Craig and was seeking legal advice to ensure that his statement of defence complied with court rules for defamation cases. However, Craig's lawsuit against Stringer and Jordan Williams' lawsuit against Craig remained ongoing.{{cite news|last1=Van Breynen|first1=Martin|title=John Stringer dumps claim against Colin Craig in Christchurch defamation action|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/77468166/John-Stringer-dumps-claim-against-Colin-Craig-in-Christchurch-defamation-action|access-date=11 April 2016|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=2 March 2016}} In September 2016, the [[Auckland High Court]] began hearing Jordan Williams' defamation lawsuit against Craig, expected to last five weeks.{{cite news|title=Colin Craig in court to defend defamation Action|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/312572/colin-craig-in-court-to-defend-defamation-case|access-date=6 September 2016|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]|date=5 September 2016}} On 7 September, the former party chief executive and [[Epsom (New Zealand electorate)|Epsom]] candidate [[Christine Rankin]] testified that revelations about Craig's alleged romantic impropriety with his press secretary Rachel MacGregor had led her to doubt his suitability to lead the Party.{{cite news|last1=Tahana|first1=Yvonne|title=Christine Rankin changed her opinion of Colin Craig after sext revelations, court hears|url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/christine-rankin-changed-her-opinion-colin-craig-after-sext-revelations-court-hears|access-date=15 September 2016|publisher=One News|date=7 September 2016}} On 12 September, the party's former board member John Stringer alleged that Craig had acted inappropriately toward other women and said that there had been so much concern about his relationship with MacGregor that the party had arranged a chaperone to accompany them whenever they were together. Stringer claimed in his testimony that Craig had dismissed concerns about his alleged sexual impropriety raised by the party's board. He also alleged that Craig had created a "cult-like" atmosphere within the Conservative Party and that Craig had disciplined, harassed, and denigrated members who had disagreed with him. Stringer denied Craig's assertions that there was a "Dirty Politics" strategy within the party to unseat him and claimed that the party had lost confidence in their leader.{{cite news|last1=Hollingworth|first1=Adam|title=Colin Craig needed chaperone around MacGregor – Stringe|url=http://www.newshub.co.nz/nznews/colin-craig-needed-chaperone-around-macgregor---stringer-2016091212|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160913164632/http://www.newshub.co.nz/nznews/colin-craig-needed-chaperone-around-macgregor---stringer-2016091212|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 September 2016|access-date=15 September 2016|publisher=[[Newshub]] |date=12 September 2016}} On 14 and 15 September, MacGregor testified that Craig's alleged harassment during the three years of her employment had contributed to her decision to resign two days prior to the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]]. In her testimony, she cited a pay dispute as the final straw in her decision to resign.{{cite news|last1=Dennett|first1=Kelly|title=Rachel MacGregor's text messages to Colin Craig read to court|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/84256582/former-conservative-leader-colin-craig-under-huge-pressure-lawyers-say|access-date=15 September 2016|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=14 September 2016}} On 16 September, Colin Craig took the stand to testify in his defence. While denying that he sexually harassed MacGregor, Craig likened their relationship to that of siblings. He also admitted kissing her but insisted it was consensual. In his defence, Craig claimed that MacGregor had resigned primarily because he had rejected her marriage proposal on the grounds that he was already married.{{cite news|last1=Fagan|first1=Josh|title=Colin Craig denies sexual harassment, explicit texts, but admits there was a kiss|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/84324546/colin-craig-denies-sexual-harassment-explicit-texts-but-admits-there-was-a-kiss|access-date=16 September 2016|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=16 September 2016}}{{cite news|title=Did she think I would leave my wife?|url=http://m.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11711164|access-date=16 September 2016|publisher=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=16 September 2016}} On 20 September, Craig's wife Helen Craig testified that MacGregor had privately contacted her to confess to having an emotional relationship with Craig and kissing Craig on the night of the 2011 general election. Helen also confirmed that she had forgiven her husband.{{cite news|last1=Dennett|first1=Kelly|title=Court hears of 'relationship rules' between Rachel MacGregor and Colin Craig|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/84440974/macgregor-took-restraining-order-against-colin-craig-associate|access-date=20 September 2016|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=20 September 2016}} While Craig had admitted kissing McGregor, he denied undressing or having sexual intercourse with her.{{cite news|last1=Leask|first1=Anna|title=Colin Craig on kiss with press secretary|url=http://m.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11713454|access-date=20 September 2016|publisher=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=20 September 2016}} On 21 September, the investigative journalist [[Nicky Hager]] testified as an expert witness. In his testimony, he alleged that the information that had been released about Colin Craig on blogs like Cameron Slater's Whale Oil matched the patterns he had documented in his book ''[[Dirty Politics]]'', which had inspired Craig's pamphlet "Dirty Politics and Hidden Agendas".{{cite news|last1=Leask|first1=Anna|title=Colin Craig defamation trial: Dirty Politics author Nicky Hager takes the stand|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11714115|access-date=21 September 2016|publisher=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=21 September 2016}} Brian Dobbs, the former chairman of the Conservative Party, also testified that he and several other board members had expressed their dissatisfaction with Craig's and MacGregor's relationship. He criticised Craig for proceeding with the 2015 sauna interview without consulting him first. Dobbs disclosed that Williams had shown him a collection of love letters, poems, emails, and other correspondence between Craig and MacGregor in June 2015 in an alleged attempt to turn him against Craig. Dobbs also criticised MacGregor's resignation for contributing to the party's disappointing performance in the 2011 general election.{{cite news|title=Colin Craig defamation trial: Nicky Hager gives evidence|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/national/313866/colin-craig-defamation-trial-hager-gives-evidence|access-date=22 September 2016|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=21 September 2016}} On 22 September, former Conservative Party board member Laurence Day disputed MacGregor's claim that Colin Craig had sexually harassed her, on the grounds that Williams had failed to present the incriminating alleged "sext" text message. He also alleged that Williams was trying to use the sexual harassment allegations to turn the party board members against Craig; a position that was echoed by another witness, [[Family First New Zealand|Family First]] director [[Bob McCoskrie]]. Day and McCoskrie supported Craig's assertion that his relationship with MacGregor had been inappropriate but consensual. McCoskrie defended Craig's pamphlet as a response to the alleged "organized campaign" against Craig.{{cite news|last1=Dennett|first1=Kelly|title=Former Conservative board member says a male secretary wouldn't have flattered Colin Craig|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/84531305/family-first-director-bob-mccoskrie-says-colin-craigs-poetry-bad|access-date=22 September 2016|agency=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=22 September 2016}} On 23 September, several Conservative Party staff members including Bev Adair-Beets, Angela Storr, and Kevin Stitt disputed MacGregor's sexual harassment allegations against Craig and vouched for the accuracy of Craig's allegations in his "Dirty Politics" pamphlet. While Jordan Williams' lawyer Peter Knight cited the letters and poems as evidence of Craig's alleged sexual harassment against MacGregor, Craig's lawyer Stephen Mills [[Queen's Counsel|QC]] asserted that Craig had the right to defend himself through his "Dirty Politics" pamphlet. Mills also contended that Williams had broken MacGregor's trust by passing information on her relationship with Craig to other Conservative Party officials and [[Cameron Slater]]'s blog Whale Oil.{{cite news|title=Colin Craig trial: 'Jordan Williams wanted leader gone'|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11718475|access-date=28 September 2016|publisher=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=28 September 2016}}{{cite news|title=Colin Craig's lawyer makes final push to clear his name|url=http://www.newshub.co.nz/politics/colin-craigs-lawyer-makes-final-push-to-clear-his-name-2016092811|access-date=28 September 2016|publisher=[[Newshub]] |date=28 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160928154201/http://www.newshub.co.nz/politics/colin-craigs-lawyer-makes-final-push-to-clear-his-name-2016092811|archive-date=28 September 2016|url-status=dead}} On 30 September, the eleven-member jury unanimously ruled against Craig in Jordan Williams' favour. October 2020|url-status=live}} ===Elliot Ikilei era, November to December 2020=== [[File:Elliot_Ikilei.jpeg|thumb|[[Elliot Ikilei]], party leader November–December 2020]]Following the 2020 election, the party's board replaced Baker as leader with his deputy, [[Elliot Ikilei]], on 19 November. The chair of the board, Simon Gutschlag, wrote in a newsletter to the party's followers that the board had conducted a review of the leadership and had decided "to look for a fresh approach," which meant "relieving" Baker of his role. Baker posted a statement on Twitter where he described his departure as "a tough day at the office," but wished the new leadership well. Victoria O'Brien, a gun advocate who had been third on the party's list at the 2020 election, succeeded Ikilei as deputy leader.{{cite news |last1=Small |first1=Zane |title=No-nonsense' gun advocate Victoria O'Brien part of New Conservative's fresh leadership team as Leighton Baker departs |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/11/no-nonsense-gun-advocate-victoria-o-brien-part-of-new-conservative-s-fresh-leadership-team-as-leighton-baker-departs.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201127060238/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/11/no-nonsense-gun-advocate-victoria-o-brien-part-of-new-conservative-s-fresh-leadership-team-as-leighton-baker-departs.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 November 2020 |access-date=19 November 2020 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=19 November 2020}} Ikilei complimented his predecessor's devotion to the party and conservative politics while signalling that he would bring a "more aggressive and “confrontational” approach to presentation style."{{cite news|title= Leighton Baker steps down as New Conservative leader|url= https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/leighton-baker-steps-down-new-conservative-leader |access-date=19 November 2020 |publisher=[[1News]]|date=19 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201119040831/https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/leighton-baker-steps-down-new-conservative-leader|archive-date=19 November 2020|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|last=Braae|first=Alex|date=19 November 2020|title=Coup Conservatives? Leader ousted to make way for 'outspoken' Elliot Ikilei|url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/19-11-2020/coup-conservatives-leader-ousted-to-make-way-for-outspoken-elliot-ikilei/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201119043106/https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/19-11-2020/coup-conservatives-leader-ousted-to-make-way-for-outspoken-elliot-ikilei/|archive-date=19 November 2020|access-date=19 November 2020|work=[[The Spinoff]]}} Less than a week after the leadership change, on 25 November, O'Brien resigned the deputy leadership, saying in a social media post that her decision was "due to a growing divergence between the direction of the party and my beliefs and values.” She later said that she had left because of Leighton Baker's "ongoing involvement with the party." Her announcement occurred in the context of some discontent from party supporters at Baker's removal, which had taken many by surprise. It was declared that deputy leadership would be vacant until a process to fill the role is put in place in early 2021,{{cite news |last1=Braae |first1=Alex |title=New Conservative deputy quits one week in, deepening leadership tumult |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/25-11-2020/new-conservative-deputy-quits-one-week-in-deepening-leadership-tumult/ |access-date=25 November 2020 |publisher=[[The Spinoff]] |date=25 November 2020}} however, as of 2026, no successor has been chosen. On 31 December 2020, Ikilei announced on his Twitter account that he was resigning as leader of the New Conservatives.{{cite tweet|user=ElliotIkilei|number=1344278514262921216 |date=31 December 2020|title=Resignation}} ===Helen Houghton and Ted Johnston era, October 2021–2023=== On 11 October 2021, the party's board announced Helen Houghton and Ted Johnston as interim co-leaders. Houghton is from Christchurch and of European descent.{{cite news |author1=New Conservative Party |title=New Conservative Leadership Announcement |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2110/S00075/new-conservative-leadership-announcement.htm |access-date=22 December 2021 |work=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211130175130/https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2110/S00075/new-conservative-leadership-announcement.htm|archive-date=30 November 2021|url-status=live}} She has opposed gender diversity education in schools and stood as the party's [[Christchurch East]] candidate.{{cite news |title=Teacher urges MPs to stop teaching of gender diversity in schools |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/02/teacher-urges-mps-to-stop-teaching-of-gender-diversity-in-new-zealand-schools.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929110206/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/02/teacher-urges-mps-to-stop-teaching-of-gender-diversity-in-new-zealand-schools.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 September 2020 |access-date=22 December 2021 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=12 February 2021}} Johnston is from Auckland and of European and [[Samoan people|Samoan]] descent. He is also a criminal lawyer, a former candidate for [[The Opportunities Party]], and a mayoral candidate during the [[2019 Auckland mayoral election]].{{cite news |title=Points of Order: A pre-Christmas panic descends on Parliament, and for Judith Collins' opponents there's an early present |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/127116128/points-of-order-a-prechristmas-panic-descends-on-parliament-and-for-judith-collins-opponents-theres-an-early-present |access-date=22 December 2021 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=27 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127020005/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/127116128/points-of-order-a-prechristmas-panic-descends-on-parliament-and-for-judith-collins-opponents-theres-an-early-present|archive-date=27 November 2021|url-status=live}}{{cite news |last1=Franks |first1=Josephine |title=Auckland mayoral race: Ted 'Rocky' Johnston throws hat in the ring with shoestring budget |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/115336637/auckland-mayoral-race-ted-rocky-johnston-throws-hat-in-the-ring-with-shoestring-budget |access-date=22 December 2021 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=28 August 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211126224445/https://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/115336637/auckland-mayoral-race-ted-rocky-johnston-throws-hat-in-the-ring-with-shoestring-budget |archive-date=26 November 2021|url-status=live}} Houghton and Johnston have said that they are attempting to make the party more attractive to centrist New Zealanders. For the [[2022 Hamilton West by-election]], New Conservative announced that it joined with the [[ONE Party|One Party]] to stand a single candidate: Rudi du Plooy, a New Conservative Party member.{{cite news |last1=Franke-Bowell |first1=Jonah |date=7 November 2022 |title=One candidate, two parties: Conservative coalition picks Hamilton West contender |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/waikato-times/news/300732811/one-candidate-two-parties-conservative-coalition-picks-hamilton-west-contender |access-date=7 November 2022}} Du Plooy gained 118 votes in that contest, which meant that he came seventh overall.{{cite web |title=Hamilton West by-election official results |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2022/hamilton-west-by-election-official-results/ |website=elections.nz |publisher=Electoral Commission |access-date=4 February 2023 |date=21 December 2022 |language=en-NZ}} ===2023 general election=== On 2 September 2023, Ted Johnston announced he had left the New Conservatives to form the [[Unity Party (New Zealand)|Unity Party]],{{Cite web |last=T-Pole |first=Marama |date=2 September 2023 |title=New Conservative co-leader announces he's leaving party |url=https://tpplus.co.nz/news-politics/talanoa-new-conservative-co-leader-announces-hes-leaving-party/ |access-date=6 June 2026 |website=[[Tagata Pasifika]]}} which allied with the [[Democratic Alliance (New Zealand)|Democratic Alliance]] for the {{NZ election link|2023}}.{{cite web |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2309/S00035/the-democratic-alliance-is-the-new-hope-for-new-zealanders.htm |title=The 'Democratic Alliance' Is The New Hope For New Zealanders |date=6 September 2023 |website=Scoop.co.nz}}{{Primary source inline|date=November 2023}} In August 2023, the New Conservative's leader Helen Houghton released the party's Family Builder policy, which was costed at NZ$9.1 billion in its first year. Key provisions included allowing workers to keep the first $20,000 they earned, child tax credits, allowing couples to split their income, and shifting funding from early childhood centres to parents with the goal of encouraging at least one parent to work from home. Houghton said that the Family Builder policy was intended to encourage parents not to split up and to protect the family unit. [[Victoria University of Wellington]] researcher [[Max Rashbrooke]] questioned the effectiveness of the party's Family Builder policy and said that reducing funding for solo parent households could harm vulnerable families.{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=David |title=New Conservative's big idea is huge tax changes aimed at families with kids |url=https://www.newsroom.co.nz/the-new-conservatives-big-idea-is-huge-tax-changes-aimed-at-families-with-kids |access-date=22 September 2023 |work=[[Newsroom (website)|Newsroom]] |date=8 August 2023}} The party received 0.15% of the party vote and won no electorates.{{Cite web |title=2023 General Election – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/index.html |website=Electoral Commission}} This was the party's worst result in any general election. ==Organisation== As of mid-2019, the New Conservative Party had 35 electorates across New Zealand covered by committees with teams of convenors and volunteer teams. The party's two main support bases at that time were around the [[Canterbury, New Zealand|Canterbury]] and [[Auckland Region]]s, where party leader Baker and deputy leader Ikilei are based. According to ''[[The Spinoff]]'' journalist Alex Braae, the New Conservatives had rebuilt a sophisticated party organisation with active campaigning, handing out pamphlets, and drink bottles with the party's logo. Based on rough figures released by party secretary Kevin Stitt, Braae estimated that the party had around 1000–1500 members. However, by the [[2023 New Zealand general election]], the New Conservative Party could only field ten candidates on its party list{{Cite web |title=2023 General Election Parties |url=https://elections.nz/democracy-in-nz/historical-events/2023-general-election/parties |access-date=12 August 2026 |website=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}} and came fourteenth in terms of total voter share.{{Cite web |date=3 November 2023 |title=Official results for the 2023 General Election |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2023/official-results-for-the-2023-general-election |access-date=12 August 2026 |website=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}} ===Youth wing=== The New Conservative Party had a youth wing called Young Conservative. The group's website described it as "a supporting youth membership of New Conservative" which "adhere[s] to the principles and policies for which New Conservative stands", and it set out the youth wing's top three policies of "Democracy, Family, and Environment".{{Cite web|title=About Us|url=https://www.youngconservative.org.nz/about-us|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190203035633/https://www.youngconservative.org.nz/about-us|archive-date=3 February 2019|access-date=20 August 2020|website=Young Conservative}} However, {{As of|2020|August|lc=y}}, this website is not operating. In an interview with ''The Wireless'' in 2018, Young Conservative opposed same-sex marriage, abortion reform, and affirmative action, and sought an eventual ban on [[pornography]].{{cite news |title=New Zealand's Young Conservatives |url=http://thewireless.co.nz/articles/new-zealand-s-young-conservatives |access-date=25 July 2019 |publisher=The Wireless, [[Radio New Zealand]] |date=22 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180926152237/http://thewireless.co.nz/articles/new-zealand-s-young-conservatives |archive-date=26 September 2018}} ===Tauranga by-election: June 2022=== Helen Houghton stood for the New Conservatives in the [[Tauranga]] electorate, after former [[New Zealand National Party]] leader [[Simon Bridges]] stepped down from Parliament. She won 103 votes in all, placing eighth out of a field of twelve candidates and outpolled by the rival conservative Christian [[ONE Party]] candidate as well as the [[Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party]] candidate Tauranga by-election official results: 1 July 2022: http://elections.nz/media-and-news/2022/tauranga-by-election-official-results/ ===Auckland mayoral election: October 2022=== Ted Johnston stood for the October [[2022 Auckland mayoral election]] in October 2022.
